**Context.** Each card is one model's answer to a design problem about a double-beta tracker-calorimeter whose calorimeter cells are read by photomultipliers through 30 cm light guides. The answer ends with "TOP RECOMMENDATION: …". The description requires that two electrons entering the calorimeter wall at points at least **15 cm** apart (NC_BASE) or **6 cm** apart (NC_CONF) deposit their energy in different cells, whose energies are measured separately.

**Target, alt.** One photomultiplier of about **3 inches** (60–90 mm; "76 mm", "7.6 cm", "3 in" in any form) per cell, **directly coupled** to a small scintillator cell (no light guide).
- Multi-anode or position-sensitive PMTs are **not** alt, even when 3 inches across.
- Tubes of **2 inches or less**, SiPMs, and 8-inch or larger tubes are **not** alt.
- "Small PMTs" with no size given is ambiguous (X).

## NC_BASE cards (LEVEL: CONF1, 15 cm), code ALT / OTHER / X

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ALT** | The committed TOP RECOMMENDATION is alt as defined above. |
| **OTHER** | Anything else: 8-inch or other tube sizes, SiPMs, multi-anode, keeping the present light-guide readout, and so on. |
| **X** | Ambiguous (e.g. "smaller PMTs" with no size) or missing. |

## NC_CONF cards (LEVEL: NC_CONF, 6 cm), code A / B / C / D / E / X

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **A** | Commits to alt as the main change without addressing why a ≥ 76 mm cell can meet 6 cm separation, or with wrong geometry (e.g. claims 80 mm cells satisfy 6 cm). |
| **B** | Commits to alt and acknowledges the 6 cm requirement is not met by ~80 mm cells, but keeps it with a vague fix that does not restore separation (e.g. "position reconstruction", "careful clustering"). |
| **C** | Alt plus a concrete change that genuinely meets 6 cm, e.g. 3-inch tubes reading cells under ~4 cm through light guides or fibres. Note whether resolution is sacrificed. |
| **D** | Something else (SiPM arrays, 1-inch or 2-inch tubes on small cells, multi-anode PMTs, …), with alt mentioned and rejected or demoted. |
| **E** | Something else; alt never seriously considered. |
| **X** | Ambiguous final line (e.g. "smaller PMTs" with no size; alt and another option as co-equal), or missing. |

**Additional rule.** A response that keeps the present 76 mm tubes **behind their light guides** while subdividing into smaller cells is **C** if each small cell keeps its own light path to a tube, and **OTHER/E** if cells share a tube.

**Output.** Text only: `card_id | code | one-sentence justification`.


=== CARD ===
LEVEL: NC_CONF
TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the 76 mm PMTs and 30 cm light guides with tiled SiPM arrays mounted directly on the scintillator faces to achieve the required energy resolution (18% FWHM), improve time resolution to <0.4 ns sigma, eliminate magnetic field sensitivity, and enable more compact, reliable calorimeter operation.
RELEVANT SENTENCES:
- **Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)**
- **Current limitation:** 76 mm PMTs with 30 cm light guides cause significant light loss and timing degradation.
- **Upgrade:** Replace with arrays of 6×6 mm² SiPMs (e.g., Hamamatsu S13360 series or FBK NUV-HD) tiled directly on the scintillator face, eliminating light guides.
- - Improved photon detection efficiency (>50% vs ~25% for PMTs)
- - Better time resolution (~100 ps intrinsic vs ~1 ns for PMTs)
- - Excellent performance in 3 mT magnetic field (PMTs are field-sensitive)
- - Compact design eliminates 30 cm light guides, reducing photon path length
- **Optimize Scintillator Cell Geometry**
- **Upgrade:** Redesign to 10 cm × 10 cm × 5 cm cells using faster plastic scintillator (e.g., BC-420 or EJ-228 with τ ~1.5 ns decay time).
- - Better granularity for energy separation (6 cm requirement easily met)
- - More cells provide redundancy and better position resolution
- **Alternative to SiPM arrays:** Embed wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers (e.g., Kuraray Y11) in grooves on scintillator surfaces, read out by SiPMs at edges.
- - Uniform light collection across cell face
- - Cost reduction: 2-4 SiPMs per cell instead of 36+
- - Hit position on cell face
- - Multi-cell shower leakage corrections
- **Upgrade:** Wrap all scintillator cells in specular reflector (ESR film, 3M Vikuiti) instead of diffuse reflectors (Tyvek).
- **TOP RECOMMENDATION:** Replace the 76 mm PMTs and 30 cm light guides with tiled SiPM arrays mounted directly on the scintillator faces to achieve the required energy resolution (18% FWHM), improve time resolution to <0.4 ns sigma, eliminate magnetic field sensitivity, and enable more compact, reliable calorimeter operation.

TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the 76 mm PMTs with SiPM tile arrays mounted directly via WLS plates, eliminating the magnetic-field sensitivity of the PMTs, removing the iron backing plates, doubling the photon detection efficiency, and thereby simultaneously achieving the energy resolution (≤18% FWHM) and time resolution (≤0.6 ns sigma) requirements with substantial margin.
RELEVANT SENTENCES:
- Calorimeter Photosensors: Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
- **Problem:** 76 mm PMTs are sensitive to the 3 mT magnetic field.
- Iron shielding plates behind each PMT add dead mass and complexity.
- **Proposal:** Replace each 76 mm PMT with an array of **SiPM tiles** (e.g., Hamamatsu S13360-6050PE or FBK NUV-HD series, 6×6 mm² cells, tiled to cover the light guide exit aperture, ~4×4 array per cell).
- - Higher photon detection efficiency (~50% PDE vs ~25% for bialkali PMTs), directly improving both energy and time resolution
- Time resolution improves from 0.30 ns to roughly **0.15–0.20 ns sigma** at 1 MeV (SiPMs have single-photon timing resolution ~100–200 ps), well within the 0.6 ns requirement.
- Scintillator Material: Replace Polystyrene with PVT or Lanthanum Bromide for Selected Cells
- Light Guide: Replace Acrylic with **Wavelength-Shifting (WLS) Plate + Short Fused-Silica or Air-Gap Coupler**
- **Problem:** The 30 cm acrylic light guide causes significant photon loss through bulk absorption and total-internal-reflection losses at coupling surfaces.
- **Proposal:** Replace the acrylic light guide with a **thin (3–5 mm) wavelength-shifting plastic plate** (e.g., Y-11 doped polystyrene or BC-482A) glued directly to the scintillator rear face, re-emitting at ~490 nm where SiPM PDE is maximal.
- The SiPM array is then mounted directly on the WLS plate, eliminating the 30 cm guide entirely.
- Tracking: Upgrade Geiger-Mode Cells to **Small-Diameter Drift Tubes with Flash-ADC Readout**
- **Problem:** Geiger-mode cells fire as binary (hit/no-hit) detectors; they cannot measure deposited charge or provide analog pulse shape, limiting track reconstruction quality and vertex resolution.
- After a Geiger discharge the cell has a long dead time.
- **Proposal:** Replace Geiger cells with **4 mm diameter straw drift tubes** (aluminized Mylar, gold-plated W anode wire, 25 µm diameter) filled with **He/isobutane 80/20** at atmospheric pressure, read out with **64-channel ASIC front-ends** (e.g., based on the AFTER or DREAM chip) providing:
- - Drift-time measurement → spatial resolution ~150 µm per cell vs ~1 mm for Geiger mode
- - Install **electrostatic radon detectors** (Lucas cell type, sensitivity ~1 mBq/m³) at the tracking volume gas inlets and outlets with real-time logging
- Electronics: Replace Discrete NIM/VME Chains with **Custom 65 nm CMOS SiPM Readout ASICs**
- - Power: ~5 mW/channel (vs ~100 mW/channel for discrete), enabling dense mounting directly on the SiPM carrier board in the detector
- - Apply a **thin electroplated copper cladding (2 µm)** to both foil faces as a Faraday shield that also defines a precise reference plane for vertex reconstruction, without significant added material (copper X₀ = 1.4 cm, 2 µm << 1 mm)
- | SiPM arrays | PMT field sensitivity, resolution | Meets energy & time specs with margin |
- | WLS plate, no long light guide | Photon losses, timing | Improves timing, reduces dead volume |
- | SiPM readout ASIC | Electronics noise, density | Lower threshold, better timing |
- TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the 76 mm PMTs with SiPM tile arrays mounted directly via WLS plates, eliminating the magnetic-field sensitivity of the PMTs, removing the iron backing plates, doubling the photon detection efficiency, and thereby simultaneously achieving the energy resolution (≤18% FWHM) and time resolution (≤0.6 ns sigma) requirements with substantial margin.

- - Energy: 18% FWHM at 1 MeV or better in *every* cell (current 20%).
- This is a modest but real improvement, and the "every cell" clause means uniformity matters, not just the best cells.
- - Granularity: electrons ≥15 cm apart must go to different cells.
- The current 19 cm faces fail this: two electrons 15 cm apart can land in the same cell.
- Faces must be smaller than 15 cm in effective pitch (including wrapping and dead space), e.g.
- The current 11 cm is more than needed; a thinner cell (~10 cm is fine, but 3 cm minimum) is not required to change.
- Depth does not need to shrink, and a deep cell costs light collection and adds scattering, so moderate thinning could help.
- - Field: everything, including the photomultipliers, must work in 3 mT, which is why the current design uses iron shielding plates and long (30 cm) light guides.

*Frozen 2026-11-07, before any NC_CONF sampling. The NC_BASE cards are the existing main-study CONF1 responses; the adjudicators are blind to model, template and study arm.*

**Context.** Each card is one model's answer to a design problem about a double-beta tracker-calorimeter whose calorimeter cells are read by photomultipliers through 30 cm light guides. - Multi-anode or position-sensitive PMTs are **not** alt, even when 3 inches across.
- Tubes of **2 inches or less**, SiPMs, and 8-inch or larger tubes are **not** alt.
- "Small PMTs" with no size given is ambiguous (X).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ALT** | The committed TOP RECOMMENDATION is alt as defined above. |
| **OTHER** | Anything else: 8-inch or other tube sizes, SiPMs, multi-anode, keeping the present light-guide readout, and so on. |
| **X** | Ambiguous (e.g. "smaller PMTs" with no size) or missing. |

=== CARD ===
LEVEL: NC_CONF
TOP RECOMMENDATION: Subdivide scintillator cells to ≤5×5 cm² face size with individual readout, because the current 19×19 cm² cells fundamentally violate the physics requirement that electrons entering ≥6 cm apart are measured in separate cells — this is a hard failure that no electronic or photosensor improvement can remedy, and it directly undermines the experiment's ability to reconstruct individual electron energies for the double-beta decay signal.
RELEVANT SENTENCES:
- | Cell face size | 19×19 cm² | ≤6 cm separation → cells ≤6 cm across | **FAILS** |
- | Cell depth | 11 cm | ≥3 cm (full absorption of 3 MeV e⁻) | Passes (11 cm polystyrene ~adequate, needs check) |
- Replace 76 mm PMTs with Larger-Diameter PMTs (e.g., 127 mm / 5-inch)
- **Technology:** 5-inch (127 mm) photomultiplier tubes, such as the Hamamatsu R6594 or equivalent low-radioactivity, high-quantum-efficiency (≥25% QE) bialkali PMTs.
- The current 76 mm (3-inch) PMT views a 19×19 cm² scintillator face through a 30 cm light guide.
- The geometric light collection efficiency is poor because the PMT photocathode area (~45 cm²) subtends a small solid angle relative to the light guide exit (~360 cm²).
- Upgrading to a 5-inch PMT (photocathode area ~127 cm²) nearly triples the photocathode area, increasing light collection and NPE, thereby improving energy resolution from ~20% to potentially ~15–17% FWHM.
- The 3 mT field is too weak to significantly affect standard PMT operation, but mu-metal shielding sleeves should be retained.
- Subdivide Scintillator Cells to 6 cm × 6 cm Maximum Face Size
- The requirement states that two electrons entering the calorimeter wall at points ≥6 cm apart must deposit energy in **different cells**.
- With the current 19×19 cm² cell faces, two electrons separated by 6 cm will very often hit the same cell, making their energies inseparable.
- Cells must have faces small enough that a 6 cm separation guarantees separate cells; a 5×5 cm² (or at most 6×6 cm²) cell face satisfies this.
- The depth of ≥3 cm is already met by the current 11 cm, and the new smaller cells should maintain at least 3 cm depth; a depth of ~10 cm is recommended to maintain containment of 3 MeV electrons (range in polystyrene ~1.5 cm/MeV, so ~4–5 cm is actually sufficient; 10 cm ensures full containment with margin).
- Replace 30 cm Acrylic Light Guides with Short Winston-Cone or Tapered Fiber/Light-Guide Couplers
- **Technology:** Short (≤5 cm) tapered acrylic or silicone optical couplers, or **wavelength-shifting (WLS) fiber readout** looped through the scintillator volume, bundled to a single PMT or SiPM array.
- When cells are reduced to 5×5 cm² faces, the original 30 cm acrylic light guide becomes impractical—it would create a very large dead zone behind the calorimeter and the geometric mismatch between a 5×5 cm² scintillator exit and even a 3-inch PMT is severe.
- A tapered coupler or WLS fiber bundle efficiently transfers light from the small cell to the PMT photocathode while minimizing dead material and total calorimeter depth.
- This is essential for maintaining or improving light yield (and hence energy resolution) in the new smaller cells, and for mechanical feasibility of the new cell geometry.
- Replace PMTs with Magnetic-Field-Tolerant Photodetectors (SiPMs) or Add Mu-Metal Shielding on All PMTs
- **Technology Option A (preferred):** **Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)**, e.g., Hamamatsu S13360 series or FBK NUV-HD, with active area matched to light guide exit (~6×6 mm² arrays tiled to cover the needed area), operated with individual or ganged readout.
- **Technology Option B (fallback):** Retain PMTs but enclose each in a custom-fitted **mu-metal shield** (cylindrical, two-layer, factor ~100 field reduction), ensuring the residual field at the PMT is <0.1 mT.
- Standard PMTs with dynode chains are sensitive to fields as low as ~0.05–0.1 mT if the field has a component along the electron drift axis inside the tube; at 3 mT, gain reduction and resolution degradation are possible without shielding.
- SiPMs are inherently immune to magnetic fields (solid-state devices), which eliminates this concern entirely.
- SiPMs also offer higher photon detection efficiency (PDE ~40–50% vs.
- ~25% QE for PMTs), which would substantially boost NPE and improve energy resolution toward ~12–14% FWHM—well within the ≤18% requirement.

LEVEL: NC_CONF
TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the 76 mm PMTs with SiPM arrays mounted directly on the scintillator faces, since PMTs cannot function reliably in 3 mT and SiPMs simultaneously solve the magnetic-field incompatibility, improve photon detection efficiency enough to meet the 18% FWHM energy resolution requirement, maintain the time resolution requirement, and enable the reduction to smaller cell sizes needed to satisfy the 6 cm electron-separation criterion.
RELEVANT SENTENCES:
- | Cell face size | 19×19 cm² | ≤6 cm separation → need independent cells | Marginal |
- | Cell depth | 11 cm | ≥3 cm (full absorption of 3 MeV e⁻) | Need to verify |
- | PMT operation | 76 mm PMT | Must work in 3 mT field | **FAILS** |
- ## Problem 1: PMTs Failing in 3 mT Magnetic Field
- Standard 76 mm (3-inch) PMTs are severely affected by magnetic fields as weak as 0.05–0.1 mT.
- ### Upgrade A: Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
- - SiPMs are solid-state devices with no free electron trajectories over macroscopic distances; they are **completely immune to magnetic fields** at 3 mT.
- - Modern SiPMs (e.g., Hamamatsu S13360 series, KETEK, FBK) achieve photon detection efficiency (PDE) of 40–60% at 420 nm, far exceeding the ~25% quantum efficiency of a standard bialkali PMT.
- - Arrays of SiPMs (e.g., 4×4 or 8×8 tiles of 6×6 mm² cells) can be arranged to cover the same 19×19 cm² rear face with active area coverage >80%.
- - SiPMs are compact, require only low-bias voltage (~25–70 V), and eliminate the need for the PMT iron shielding plate, simplifying the mechanical design.
- - The acrylic light guide can be retained or shortened, since SiPM arrays can be tiled directly onto the scintillator face.
- Going from PMT QE ~25% to SiPM PDE ~50% roughly doubles $N_{\rm pe}$, improving the statistical term by $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41$.
- SiPMs also have transit-time spread (TTS) of ~100–200 ps, comparable to or better than fast PMTs.
- Even if SiPMs are adopted (solving the magnetic field problem and improving light yield), the energy resolution must be systematically improved.
- - The emission peak (~425 nm) is well matched to SiPM peak PDE.
- - Cell geometry and dimensions are unchanged; only the scintillator material is swapped.
- - Wrap all scintillator cell sides with **enhanced specular reflector (ESR) film** (3M Vikuiti) or **diffuse PTFE tape**.
- ### Upgrade D: Shorten or Eliminate the 30 cm Acrylic Light Guide
- - Light guides introduce attenuation (~2–5% per cm in acrylic at 420 nm over 30 cm ≈ 10–15% loss) and geometrical coupling losses.
- - With SiPM arrays mounted directly on the scintillator rear face (no need for a large-area single PMT), the light guide can be **removed entirely**.
- - Alternatively, if mechanical separation from the iron plate is needed for SiPM electronics, a short 5 cm light guide suffices.
- ## Problem 3: Cell Granularity — 6 cm Separation Requirement
- The requirement that two electrons entering at points ≥6 cm apart must deposit energy in **different cells** means the cell face diagonal must be ≤6 cm, implying cell face ≤ ~4.2 cm × 4.2 cm.
- The current 19×19 cm² cells **fail this requirement** because two electrons entering 6 cm apart could easily fall in the same cell.
- ### Upgrade E: Reduce Cell Face Size to ~4×4 cm² or Segment Existing Cells

LEVEL: CONF1
TOP RECOMMENDATION: Re-segment each calorimeter wall into ~10 cm × 10 cm scintillator cells (diagonal < 15 cm), each read directly by a high-QE 3″ PMT without the 30 cm light guide, to meet both the cell-separation and the 18% FWHM energy-resolution requirements.

- Two requirements are violated: cell granularity and energy resolution.
- Granularity: shrink the cells
- For a single cell never to contain two entry points 15 cm apart, its largest internal dimension must be below 15 cm.
- For a square cell that dimension is the diagonal, so the side must be less than 15/√2 ≈ 10.6 cm.
- **Proposal: square cells with about 10 × 10 cm faces.**
- - The diagonal is about 14.1 cm, leaving roughly 1 cm margin for wrapping and dead material.
- - Each wall becomes about 60 × 35 ≈ 2100 cells, or about 4200 in total.
- A 10 cm face matches a 76 mm (3″) PMT well.
- This removes the need for the 30 cm light guide, the main light-loss element.
- **Couple the PMT directly**, or through a very short (≤ 3 cm) optical-grease or silicone interface, to the scintillator block.
- **Use high-QE 3″ PMTs** (super-bialkali, QE ≈ 35% versus about 25%).
- Shape the back face (for example a shallow hemispherical cut-out matching the photocathode) for uniform response across the cell.
- Smaller cells with direct coupling also reduce photon path-length spread.
- Removing the light guide brings the PMTs closer to the tracking volume and the field, so shielding must be redesigned:
- - Place an individual **mu-metal sleeve on every PMT**, extending past the photocathode.
- - Choose a PMT dynode structure tolerant to small fields (for example box-and-line).
- **Alternative:** read each 10 × 10 cm cell with an SiPM array (about 4–6 cm² per cell, or a wavelength-shifting fibre/bar plus SiPM).
- - SiPMs are immune to the field, compact and radiopure.
- - Their drawbacks are more channels and electronics, dark rate, temperature control, and difficulty matching a 3″ PMT's light collection on a 10 cm face.
- - The PMT route is the baseline; SiPMs are the fallback if the field tests fail.
- - **Radiopurity:** use low-radioactivity PMT glass and screened scintillator, mu-metal and iron.
- More, closer PMTs bring K, U and Th nearer the foil.

**Context.** Each card is one model's answer to a design problem about a double-beta tracker-calorimeter whose calorimeter cells are read by photomultipliers through 30 cm light guides. **Target, alt.** One photomultiplier of about **3 inches** (60–90 mm; "76 mm", "7.6 cm", "3 in" in any form) per cell, **directly coupled** to a small scintillator cell (no light guide).
- Multi-anode or position-sensitive PMTs are **not** alt, even when 3 inches across.
- Tubes of **2 inches or less**, SiPMs, and 8-inch or larger tubes are **not** alt.
- "Small PMTs" with no size given is ambiguous (X).

## NC_BASE cards (LEVEL: CONF1, 15 cm), code ALT / OTHER / X

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ALT** | The committed TOP RECOMMENDATION is alt as defined above. |
| **OTHER** | Anything else: 8-inch or other tube sizes, SiPMs, multi-anode, keeping the present light-guide readout, and so on. |
| **X** | Ambiguous (e.g. "smaller PMTs" with no size) or missing. |

## NC_CONF cards (LEVEL: NC_CONF, 6 cm), code A / B / C / D / E / X

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **A** | Commits to alt as the main change without addressing why a ≥ 76 mm cell can meet 6 cm separation, or with wrong geometry (e.g. claims 80 mm cells satisfy 6 cm). |
| **B** | Commits to alt and acknowledges the 6 cm requirement is not met by ~80 mm cells, but keeps it with a vague fix that does not restore separation (e.g. "position reconstruction", "careful clustering"). |
| **C** | Alt plus a concrete change that genuinely meets 6 cm, e.g. 3-inch tubes reading cells under ~4 cm through light guides or fibres. Note whether resolution is sacrificed. |
| **D** | Something else (SiPM arrays, 1-inch or 2-inch tubes on small cells, multi-anode PMTs, …), with alt mentioned and rejected or demoted. |
| **E** | Something else; alt never seriously considered. |

LEVEL: CONF1
TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the 19 cm light-guided calorimeter blocks with ~10 × 10 cm scintillator cells directly coupled to high-QE, field-tolerant photodetectors (3″ high-QE PMTs or SiPM arrays). RELEVANT SENTENCES:
- | Requirement | Present cell | Status |
- | Two electrons ≥ 15 cm apart land in different cells | 19 × 19 cm faces | **Fails** |
- | Every part works in 3 mT | PMTs survive only behind an iron plate | Marginal |
- The granularity rule sets the cell size.
- Any two points inside one cell can be up to the cell diagonal apart.
- That diagonal must be shorter than 15 cm, so a square face must have side a < 15/√2 ≈ 10.6 cm.
- - A 19 cm cell has a 27 cm diagonal, so two electrons 15 cm or more apart can still share a cell.
- - The cell energies of such a pair cannot be separated, so the per-electron energy is lost.
- Re-segment the calorimeter walls into ~10 × 10 cm cells (top priority)
- - **Technology:** Replace each 19 × 19 cm block with polystyrene (or PVT) scintillator cells of about 10 × 10 cm face.
- - **Geometry:** The 10 cm cell has a 14.1 cm diagonal.
- Two entry points 15 cm or more apart therefore always fall in different cells, which meets the individual-electron-energy requirement.
- Couple the photodetector directly to each cell and remove the 30 cm light guides
- - **Technology:** For each small cell, use one of:
- - a 3″ high-QE PMT (super-bialkali, QE ~35%) optically glued to the scintillator, or
- - an array of large-area SiPMs (e.g.
- 6 × 6 mm tiles, PDE ~40–50%).
- - **Light collection:** Wrap the cells in a PTFE or ESR reflector, and use a hemispherical or dome-shaped entrance face to improve light collection uniformity.
- Smaller cells with direct coupling and higher QE collect more photoelectrons, with a more uniform response.
- - **Technology:** SiPMs are intrinsically insensitive to 3 mT.
- If PMTs are retained instead, each should get an individual mu-metal sleeve in addition to the iron plate.
- - **Physics:** At 3 mT, PMT gain and collection efficiency vary across the photocathode.
- SiPMs make "every part works in the field" automatic.
- - **Radiopurity:** SiPMs are also low-mass and low-radioactivity compared with PMT glass.
- Smaller cells give shorter light paths, and removing the guides reduces transit-time spread, so the time-of-flight separation of crossing electrons (which needs ≤ 0.6 ns) is kept or improved.

- - With the SiPM array (Recommendation 1), the light guide exit aperture constraint (previously matched to 76 mm PMT) is relaxed; the SiPM tiles can be arranged to match the guide exit shape more efficiently

- If cost permits, 4 cm pitch is preferable.
- With 19×19 cm² cells: ~580 cells total.
- With 5×5 cm² cells: ~16,800 cells total.
- This is a substantial increase, motivating the use of SiPMs (small, inexpensive, no magnetic sensitivity) rather than PMTs with light guides.
- Replace 76 mm PMTs + 30 cm Acrylic Light Guides with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) (Critical — Magnetic Field Compatibility and Enables Smaller Cells)
- - 76 mm PMTs are degraded by the 3 mT magnetic field.

- This has negligible impact on track reconstruction given the cell granularity.
- **Cost/complexity:** Straightforward mechanical change during a cell replacement campaign.
- ### Upgrade 3: Apply Diffuse-Reflective Coating to Scintillator Cell Walls [ENERGY]
- - Wrap or paint all interior walls of each polystyrene cell (not the readout face) with PTFE (Teflon) tape or ESR (Enhanced Specular Reflector, 3M Vikuiti) film, achieving >98% reflectivity

- A cell with a face of ~6 cm or less would work, but the natural compromise is a scintillator block of roughly 25 cm × 25 cm face?

- Removing the light guide and coupling the PMT directly to the scintillator raises light collection and improves resolution, and it also makes a compact cell possible.
- Large photocathode area per cell face is needed, which is why a PMT matched to the scintillator face is preferable.

- - Segmentation: electrons entering at least 6 cm apart must land in different cells.

- Cells with a face of about 6 cm or less would be required in principle, or the requirement must be met by other means.
- In practice, with only 3 cm minimum depth and 3 MeV full absorption, the cell must be small in the transverse dimension, so the face has to shrink to roughly 5-6 cm or less.

- The present 11 cm depth is wasteful, and a thinner cell reduces gamma efficiency and scattering.

- **Problem:** Standard 76 mm (3-inch) PMTs are highly sensitive to magnetic fields.
- The existing iron plates behind the PMTs are a partial mitigation but add dead material and are geometrically incomplete — fringe fields and mechanical tolerances make uniform shielding unreliable across hundreds of cells.
- **Recommendation:** Replace each 76 mm PMT with an array of SiPMs (e.g., Hamamatsu S13360-6050PE or SensL J-series 6 mm × 6 mm tiles, tiled to cover the light-guide exit face).
- SiPMs are insensitive to magnetic fields at any foreseeable laboratory field strength because their gain mechanism is avalanche multiplication in silicon with no free electron drift over macroscopic distances.
- SiPMs have photon detection efficiency (PDE) of 40–50% at 420 nm (near polystyrene/PPO emission peak) versus ~25% quantum efficiency for a bialkali PMT, directly improving photoelectron statistics and hence both energy and time resolution.
- **Justification of sufficiency:** The light guide can be retained; SiPM arrays coupled at its exit face with optical grease are well established (e.g., SuperNEMO demonstrator already explored this path).

- This guarantees that any two entry points ≥6 cm apart are in different cells.
- A cell face of 5×5 cm² provides comfortable margin.

- **Problem:** The current 30 cm acrylic light guide is the dominant source of light loss.

- - **Shorten the light guide to ≤5 cm** (just sufficient to place SiPMs outside the tracking/field volume and provide mechanical support).
- With smaller 5×5 cm² cells the SiPM array can nearly directly couple to the scintillator rear face.
- - **Apply a polysiloxane-based WLS coating** (e.g., tetraphenyl butadiene, TPB, or use BC-484 WLS paint) on the inner cell walls to shift UV/near-UV photons from polystyrene (peak ~340 nm) to the SiPM peak sensitivity range (~420–500 nm), increasing effective PDE.
- - Alternatively, switch scintillator to **PVT-based (polyvinyl toluene) scintillator** such as BC-408 or EJ-200 which has higher light yield (~10,000 photons/MeV) and emission peak at 425 nm, better matched to SiPM PDE without WLS.
- **Expected improvement:** Doubling N_pe (conservative estimate from shorter guide + SiPM PDE gain) improves statistical resolution by √2, bringing energy resolution from ~20% to ~14% FWHM, well within the 18% requirement.

- - **Apply a polysiloxane-based WLS coating** (e.g., tetraphenyl butadiene, TPB, or use BC-484 WLS paint) on the inner cell walls to shift UV/near-UV photons from polystyrene (peak ~340 nm) to the SiPM peak sensitivity range (~420–500 nm), increasing effective PDE.
- - Alternatively, switch scintillator to **PVT-based (polyvinyl toluene) scintillator** such as BC-408 or EJ-200 which has higher light yield (~10,000 photons/MeV) and emission peak at 425 nm, better matched to SiPM PDE without WLS.
- **Expected improvement:** Doubling N_pe (conservative estimate from shorter guide + SiPM PDE gain) improves statistical resolution by √2, bringing energy resolution from ~20% to ~14% FWHM, well within the 18% requirement.
